Attachment

/uh-TACH-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Attachment means a feeling of affection that binds one to a person or thing; something joined or connected to something else.

Even after forty years in the city, Mr. Okafor never lost his attachment to the fishing village where he grew up.

Worked Example

Rosa felt such a deep attachment to her first violin that she kept it long after she had outgrown it.

Rosa's feeling is not about the violin's usefulness — she has outgrown it — but about the affection binding her to it. That warm, binding feeling toward a person, place, or thing is the heart of attachment.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

fondness: a warm liking for someone or something

bond: a close connection that ties people or things together

devotion: loyal, loving commitment

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

aversion: a strong dislike or desire to avoid

indifference: a lack of interest or feeling either way

Where it sits · how deeply the feeling binds you — liking → attachment → adoration

liking vs. attachment: A liking is casual — you enjoy something but could walk away; an attachment ties your heart to it.

adoration vs. attachment: Adoration burns hotter than attachment — closer to worship than to a steady, binding affection.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — at-

Prefix — at-: to, toward (assimilated form of ad-)

Root — tach-

Root — tach-: stake, fastening

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: At- ('to') + tach- ('stake, fastening') + -ment ('result of') gives attachment — originally 'the result of being staked or fastened to something,' which is exactly what a deep emotional bond feels like: your heart fastened to a person or place.

Use the root in a new word: detach

Use the root in a new word: detach: Fold along the dotted line and detach the ticket stub before entering.

Word Choice

Warm / personal

This card centers attachment's emotional sense: an affection that binds you to a person, place, or object ('a lifelong attachment to the coast'). The word also has an everyday physical sense — something joined on, like a vacuum-cleaner attachment or a file attached to an email — but when you read it in literature or on a test, the feeling sense is usually the one being tested.
